subject: Control plane egress handshake and delegation — action items & evidence
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, security-team@acme-health.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control plane egress handshake and delegation — action items & evidence

Hi team —

Following up from yesterday's sync: Acme needs explicit guidance for private deployment control-plane egress. I attached a short checklist (egress-handshake-checklist.xlsx) to make the ask concrete. Key asks from my side:

- Confirm minimal network footprint Redwood needs from Acme for the control-plane (IP allowlist + ports + protocol). Current working set below.
- Agree delegation model: Acme allows a small set of persistent NAT IPs, Redwood will provide an evidence bundle and rotation windows.
- Decide additional hardening: mTLS client certs from Redwood, SNI fingerprinting fallback, and signed request headers for audit.

Working set (proposal):
- Required outbound destinations from customer VNets: 3 IPv4 addresses (TCP 443) owned by Redwood control-plane; FQDNs: controlplane.prod.redwood.com, provisioning.redwood.net.
- TLS with client cert (mutual TLS) for management plane.
- Optional: SNI allowlist and SHA256 cert fingerprint as additional assertion for customers who cannot allow IPs directly.

Please review the checklist and confirm whether Acme's network team requires any changes. If acceptable, we will produce the runbook and an evidence PDF (SOC2 attestation excerpt + IP ownership statements).

Attachments: egress-handshake-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, security-team@acme-health.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control plane egress handshake and delegation — action items & evidence

David — thanks for the clear checklist. A couple of operational questions from CE / Ops view: 

1) Ephemeral vs stable egress IPs: many enterprise network teams insist on stable NAT IPs; others accept a published rotation window. Can we commit to a documented rotation cadence (e.g., 90-day rotation with 72-hour pre-notice) and a signed rotation history that Acme can verify?

2) Cert management: we can provide an mTLS client cert model, but for customers that can't do mTLS we should offer a SNI + cert-fingerprint fallback. Is Redwood able to publish an API endpoint for fetching current cert fingerprints (read-only) so auditors can validate?

Operational proposal: Redwood sends a signed runbook bundle (controlplane-runbook.txt) + ip-rotation PDF (egress-ip-rotation.pdf) and a short escalation matrix. I'll draft the runbook stub and attach.

Attachments: egress-ip-rotation.pdf, controlplane-runbook.txt

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Acme Security Team <security-team@acme-health.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control plane egress handshake and delegation — action items & evidence

Hi David / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the checklist. A few constraints from Acme's InfoSec that will affect the handshake design: 

- We cannot allow outbound 0.0.0.0/0 except to specifically allowlisted IPs/FQDNs with documented business justification.
- For management-plane connections we require either:
  * mTLS with certificate pinning (client certs), OR
  * IP allowlist + SNI validation with SHA256 cert fingerprints; the fingerprint must be published to a read-only, authenticated endpoint for audit.
- All control-plane sessions must be logged and retained for 12 months; we will need an exportable session/audit log from Redwood for quarterly reviews.
- Any rotation of control-plane IPs must be pre-notified 14 calendar days in writing and include the last-used IP history for the previous 12 months.

Action items we need from Redwood: 
- A runbook (step-by-step) showing the TLS handshake, certificate lifecycle, and what happens on IP rotation.
- Evidence of IP ownership (ARIN/RIPE records or signed statement).
- Point of contact for emergency revoke (phone + email).

If Redwood can provide the runbook and a short proof-of-ownership bundle we will sign a scoped network exception for the three control-plane IPs.

Regards,
Acme Health — Security Engineering
security-team@acme-health.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Acme Security Team <security-team@acme-health.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control plane egress handshake and delegation — action items & evidence

Thanks everyone — good, actionable thread. Summary and next steps so we can close the exception: 

1) Acceptance model (two-pronged):
   - Primary: Acme allowlists a small set of persistent control-plane NAT IPs (we will publish three IPv4 addresses).
   - Secondary (for segmented networks): Acme allowlists controlplane.prod.redwood.com + verifies SHA256 cert fingerprints via a read-only endpoint.

2) Hardening:
   - Mutual TLS for management plane is preferred. If the customer cannot do mTLS, we will enable SNI + certificate fingerprinting as an allowable fallback.

3) Rotation and evidence:
   - Redwood will commit to a 90-day rotation maximum with 14-day pre-notice for any IP rotation. We will publish a signed rotation log and retain last-used IPs for 12 months to meet Acme audit requirements.

4) Audit & runbook:
   - Deliverables: controlplane-runbook.txt (detailed steps), egress-ip-rotation.pdf (rotation policy), evidence bundle (IP ownership + SOC2 snippet).
   - Redwood will provide an exportable session log endpoint and a quarterly audit package.

5) Escalation / contacts:
   - Redwood emergency revoke: ops-oncall@redwood.ai / +1-415-555-0132
   - Security contact: security@redwood.ai

Action items for Acme / Legal: confirm you accept the two-pronged model above and sign the scoped network exception. I have attached a DocuSign link for the exception form; we will not start control-plane provisioning until we have the signed exception.

Attachments: controlplane-runbook.txt, egress-ip-rotation.pdf
